item.title: Major US Power Sale to Show Depth of Eastern Grid’s Tight Supply
item.description: The biggest US grid operator is about to learn how tight power supplies may get in coming years as the data-center boom sparks unprecedented electricity demand growth.

item.title: EU Plans Guidelines Next Week to Delay Methane Rules Penalties
item.description: The European Union’s executive arm wants to adopt recommendations next week delaying penalties on energy imports that fail to comply with the bloc’s controversial methane emissions regulation.

item.title: How Huawei Quietly Built a Clean Energy Leader and Found New Markets
item.description: The technology firm’s digital power unit is expanding into new markets and lifting revenue

item.title: Brazil’s First Ethanol-Powered Ship Sails in Win for Biofuels
item.description: The first container ship to run on Brazilian-made ethanol fuel is scheduled to sail early Tuesday from the port of Santos, an unprecedented test for the nation’s biofuel industry that marks a key step toward cutting emissions in maritime transportation.

item.title: London Startup Acquires Dutch Competitor in Carbon-Capture Deal
item.description: Airhive, a London-based startup, acquired its Dutch competitor, Carbyon, in a deal it says will create one of Europe’s biggest integrated direct air capture companies.

item.title: China’s Green-Tech Exports Surge on Energy Transition Demand
item.description: China’s exports of green-tech products rose by more than a third in the first half of the year, driven by the accelerating global energy transition.

item.title: Why Europeans Are Finally Warming Up to Air Conditioning
item.description: AC has long been considered an American indulgence. Heat waves are changing that.

item.title: Huawei's $11 Billion Clean Energy Empire Is Opening New Markets
item.description: Best known for telecoms infrastructure, the Chinese powerhouse has quietly become part of the backbone of the global energy transition.

item.title: After Biden Denied Alabama Coal Waste Bid, Trump Reverses Course
item.description: The Environmental Protection Agency on Monday proposed to approve Alabama’s application to take over issuing certain coal waste permits from the agency, part of a trend under President Donald Trump to transfer more authority from the federal government to states.

item.title: EU Nations to Discuss Impact of Methane Rules on Energy Security
item.description: European Union member states will this week debate the impact of the bloc’s controversial methane-emissions rules for importers on the region’s energy security.

item.title: Sunrun Offers Solar Users Hundreds Per Month in Compute Program
item.description: Sunrun Inc. is piloting a program aimed at enabling customers to earn hundreds of dollars per month that would use electricity from rooftop solar installations to power distributed computing, according to Chief Executive Officer Mary Powell.

item.title: Funding Cuts Threaten World’s Champion For Cutting Heat Deaths
item.description: Maricopa County has long been a leader and testing ground for heat-death prevention policies.

item.title: Europe Heat Wave Strains Power Grids, Hospitals and Firefighters
item.description: France is rushing air conditioners to hospitals as drought, wildfires and extreme heat grip Europe.

item.title: Climate Tech Sees Record-High Deals as Power Demand Fuels Market Appetite
item.description: The recovery in IPOs and acquisitions may help unlock fresh venture capital for the sector, experts say.

item.title: New York, US Northeast Will See Temperatures Soar This Week
item.description: New York City and the Northeast will see temperatures surge this week as another wave of sultry weather shifts across the eastern US and southern Canada.

item.title: Heat Wave Dries Up German Rhine Chokepoint to Strain Fuel Supply
item.description: Water levels at a key waypoint on the Rhine River have fallen to the lowest for the time of year in decades as Europe struggles with intense heat waves, limiting fuel flows into southern Germany and Switzerland.

item.title: Europe Battles Growing Wildfires After Relentless Heat
item.description: Wildfires are breaking out across Europe after three heat waves and weeks of low rainfall left much of the continent dangerously dry, with crews battling blazes south of Paris and in the UK, while Spain reels from one of its deadliest wildfires.

item.title: TCL Zhonghuan Buys Rival as China Aims to Reshape Solar Sector
item.description: Chinese solar wafer maker TCL Zhonghuan Renewable Energy Technology Co. has purchased a majority stake in smaller rival DAS Solar Co., the latest sign of consolidation in an industry wrought by overcapacity and a persistent supply glut.

item.title: China to See Unusually Active Typhoon Season After Bavi Passes
item.description: China may encounter stronger and more frequent tropical cyclones over the summer months, according to the national climate agency, even after Typhoon Bavi faded over the weekend without causing the widespread flooding that some forecasters had feared.

item.title: Heat Waves May Have Led to Over 2,700 Deaths in England and Wales
item.description: This summer’s heat waves may have already resulted in more than 2,700 deaths in England and Wales.

item.title: China is Supercharging a Rooftop Solar Boom in the Philippines
item.description: Soaring electricity bills are pushing Filipino households and businesses to embrace solar energy, and China is cashing in.

item.title: A Nuclear Debut in Bangladesh Tests Developing World’s Atomic Shift
item.description: A new, $13 billion Russian-built plant could generate 15% of the country's electricity.

item.title: Another Brutal Summer Tests Arizona’s Decline in Heat-Linked Deaths
item.description: Maricopa County has made progress in preventing heat-related deaths. But another scorching summer and dwindling funding threaten that trend.

item.title: Lush Grass Playing Fields for Tennis, Cricket Struggle in UK Heat
item.description: Heat waves are baking famous sports grounds.

item.title: Relentless Heat Waves Hit England’s Fabled Grass Playing Fields
item.description: When the England cricket team walks onto the field at Lord’s for a home Test, it’s to the strains of “Jerusalem,” an anthem based on a William Blake poem that extols “England’s green and pleasant land.”

item.title: China Power Load Hits Early Record as Data, EV Demand Rises
item.description: China’s nationwide electricity load reached a record high for the first time this year on July 10, hitting 1.518 billion kilowatts, the National Energy Administration said in a statement posted on its official WeChat account Saturday.

item.title: Typhoon Bavi Tracks Toward China With Heavy, Widespread Rains
item.description: A large and powerful typhoon is moving toward China, bringing heavy rain and strong winds ahead of its expected landfall later Saturday and triggering an emergency response in the Zhejiang province.

item.title: US, Kansas Settle With Keystone Pipeline Owner Over 2022 Spill
item.description: The Trump administration and the state of Kansas have settled with the owner and operator of the Keystone Pipeline over alleged violations of the Clean Water Act stemming from a 2022 oil spill.

item.title: Families in Europe’s Scorched Cities Are Being Tested By Heat
item.description: Parents face difficult choices to protect children amid punishing extreme temperatures

item.title: Western US Heat Builds as Storms Threaten Plains to Mid-Atlantic
item.description: Heat is spreading across the western US, with the most intense conditions concentrated in the central and northern Rocky Mountains and the northern Great Plains. Heat advisories, warnings and watches stretch from Nevada to northeastern Minnesota, according to the National Weather Service.
